examples.en: The teacher stresses this part.
He emphasized the importance of practice.
If you emphasize it with color, it stands out.
I underlined the words I wanted to emphasize.
There are three points to emphasize.
What the boss stressed was safety.

explain: 더 중요하다고 힘주어 말할 때 써요. 글자를 굵게 하거나 줄을 치는 것도 '강조'예요. '강조점', '강조 표시'처럼 명사로도 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 이 점을 꼭 강조하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I really want to stress this point.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 의견을 힘주어 말하고 싶을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you want to put emphasis on your own opinion.

phrases.en: I put an emphasis mark on the important words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이나 색으로 눈에 띄게 한 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a mark such as a line or color that makes something stand out.

phrases.en: The main point of this text is health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 힘주어 말하는 부분을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the part that is stressed the most.

explain_en: Use it when you stress that something is more important. Making text bold or underlining it is also '강조'. As a noun it appears in '강조점' and '강조 표시'.

examples.en: The city opened a new library.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 올해 새 전시관을 개관할 계획이에요.
examples.en: Our school plans to open a new exhibition hall this year.

examples.ko: 박물관을 개관하는 날 많은 시민이 찾아왔어요.
examples.en: Many citizens came on the day the museum opened.

examples.ko: 그 영화관은 오십 년 전에 개관했다가 얼마 전에 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: That movie theater opened fifty years ago and closed not long ago.

examples.ko: 미술관을 개관하려고 큐레이터들이 몇 달 동안 준비했어요.
examples.en: The curators prepared for months to open the art museum.

examples.ko: 개관한 지 이틀 만에 방문객이 천 명을 넘었어요.
examples.en: Within two days of opening, visitors passed a thousand.

explain: 개관하다는 도서관·박물관·미술관처럼 '관'이 붙은 곳이 처음 문을 열 때 써요. 가게·식당은 '개업하다', 병원은 '개원하다', 학교는 '개교하다'로 말이 달라요. 문을 닫는 것은 '폐관하다'예요.

phrases.example: 오늘 오후에 새 도서관 개관식이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is an opening ceremony for the new library this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 여는 것을 기념하는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The event that celebrates a place opening.

phrases.en: This library opened a long time ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 연 뒤 시간이 많이 지났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a lot of time has passed since the place opened.
phrases.en_equiv: to have been open for a long time

phrases.en: To celebrate the opening, there is no admission fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 연 것을 기념하는 행사나 혜택 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before events or benefits that mark the opening.

explain_en: 개관하다 is for a place ending in 관 (library, museum, art gallery) opening for the first time. Other places use different words: 개업하다 for shops and restaurants, 개원하다 for hospitals, 개교하다 for schools. Closing one down is 폐관하다.

examples.ko: 그 교수님은 강연에서 환경 보호의 필요성을 설파했어요.
examples.en: The professor argued strongly for the need to protect the environment in his lecture.
The pastor preaches the value of love every week.

examples.ko: 그는 평생 평화의 중요성을 설파하며 살았어요.
examples.en: He spent his whole life preaching the importance of peace.

examples.ko: 정치인이 방송에 나와 새 정책의 장점을 설파했어요.
examples.en: The politician went on TV and made the case for the benefits of the new policy.

examples.ko: 어제 친구가 채식의 장점을 한참 설파했어요.
examples.en: Yesterday my friend went on for a long time about the benefits of a vegetarian diet.

examples.ko: 이 책에서 저자는 느리게 사는 삶을 설파해요.
examples.en: In this book, the author advocates a slow way of living.

explain: '설명하다'보다 자기 생각이 옳다고 힘을 주어 말하고 믿게 하려는 느낌이 있어요. 강연, 책, 방송처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 많이 쓰고, 친구끼리는 '열심히 얘기하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: He argued for his views forcefully in his book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 생각이 옳다고 힘 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone strongly argues that their idea is right.

phrases.en: The teacher keeps stressing the importance of reading.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일의 중요함을 사람들에게 믿게 하려고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when speaking to convince people that something is important.

phrases.example: 친구가 새 영화가 얼마나 좋은지 열심히 얘기해요.
phrases.en: My friend keeps talking eagerly about how good the new movie is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때는 '설파하다' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: What you say instead of 설파하다 when talking casually with friends.

explain_en: Compared with '설명하다' (to explain), it feels more like speaking with conviction to persuade others that your view is right. It is common in lectures, books and broadcasts; among friends people would say '열심히 얘기하다'.

examples.en: The cube of 2 is 8.
If you cube 3, it becomes 27.
The unit of volume is the cubic centimeter.
We practiced cube calculations in math class.
The volume of a cube with sides of 4 is 4 cubed.
Do you know what the cubed value of the number is?

explain: '제곱'은 같은 수를 두 개 곱하는 것(3×3)이고, 세제곱은 같은 수를 세 개 곱하는 것(3×3×3)이에요. '세제곱미터', '세제곱센티미터'처럼 부피 단위에도 써요. '~를 세제곱하다'로 동사처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: If you cube 4, you get 64.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '세제곱'을 동사처럼 쓴 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun used as a verb.

phrases.en: The water in this pool is fifty cubic meters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부피를 나타내는 단위예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A unit that measures volume.

phrases.en: I poured 100 cubic centimeters of water into the cup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 부피를 말할 때 쓰는 단위예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A unit for smaller volumes.

explain_en: '제곱' means multiplying two copies of a number (3×3), while '세제곱' means multiplying three copies (3×3×3). It is also used in volume units like '세제곱미터' and '세제곱센티미터'. You can use it like a verb as in '~를 세제곱하다'.

en: easily and neatly; sinking in well

examples.en: The teacher's explanations sink right into my ears.
The child memorizes new words so quickly.

examples.ko: 이 책은 내용이 머리에 쏙쏙 들어와서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like this book because the content goes straight into my head.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 땅속으로 물이 쏙쏙 스며들어요.
examples.en: Since it rained, the water is soaking neatly into the ground.

examples.ko: 봄이 되니 새싹이 쏙쏙 올라오고 있어요.
examples.en: Now that it's spring, sprouts are popping up one after another.
This lotion soaks nicely into the skin.

explain: '쏙'은 한 번 쑥 들어가거나 빠지는 느낌이고, '쏙쏙'은 그런 일이 하나씩 계속 이어질 때 써요. 공부나 설명이 이해가 잘 될 때 '귀에 쏙쏙', '머리에 쏙쏙 들어오다'라고 많이 말해요. 칭찬하는 좋은 느낌의 말이에요.

phrases.en: When it's explained with pictures, it sinks right into my head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명이나 내용이 이해가 잘 될 때 쓰는 대표 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical expression for when an explanation is easy to understand.

phrases.example: 선생님이 예를 들어 주시니까 쏙쏙 이해돼요.
phrases.en: With the teacher giving examples, I understand things easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 내용이 하나씩 잘 이해될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when difficult content is understood smoothly, one piece at a time.

phrases.en: Water soaks into the sponge quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이나 영양이 잘 스며드는 모습에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for water or nutrients soaking in well.

explain_en: '쏙' is the feel of something going in or coming out in one smooth move, and '쏙쏙' is for that happening again and again. When studying or an explanation is easy to understand, people often say '귀에 쏙쏙' or '머리에 쏙쏙 들어오다'. It has a positive, approving feel.

examples.en: Try finding a synonym for this word.
In Korean, the synonym of the word for 'big' is the word for 'huge'.
The dictionary lists synonyms together.
Even synonyms differ a little in how they're used.
A question about choosing synonyms came up on the exam.

examples.ko: 이 말과 유의어 관계인 단어가 뭐예요?
examples.en: What word is a synonym of this one?

explain: 뜻이 비슷한 말을 가리켜요. 반대말은 '반의어'이고, '비슷한말'이라고 쉽게 말하기도 해요. 유의어라도 쓰는 상황이나 느낌이 다를 수 있어서 바꿔 쓸 때 조심해야 해요.

phrases.en: A similar word for '예쁘다' is '아름답다'.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유의어'를 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way of saying 유의어.

phrases.en: I look up unknown words in a synonym dictionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부할 때 쓰는 책이나 앱을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for books or apps used when studying.

phrases.example: 단어를 외울 때 유의어와 반의어를 같이 외워요.
phrases.en: When I memorize words, I learn synonyms and antonyms together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말과 같이 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears together with its opposite.

explain_en: It refers to words with similar meanings. The opposite is '반의어' (antonym), and people also say '비슷한말' in plain terms. Synonyms can differ in situation or feeling, so be careful when swapping them.

examples.en: I want to major in journalism at university.
The basis of journalism is checking the facts.
That reporter is famous for investigative journalism.

examples.ko: 요즘은 온라인 저널리즘이 빠르게 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: These days online journalism is growing fast.

examples.ko: 저널리즘 수업에서 기사 쓰는 법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to write news articles in my journalism class.

examples.ko: 클릭 수만 노리는 저널리즘은 비판을 받아요.
examples.en: Journalism that only chases clicks gets criticized.

explain: '언론'은 신문·방송 같은 매체나 그 활동 전체를 가리킬 때가 많고, '저널리즘'은 취재하고 보도하는 일 자체나 그 정신을 말할 때 많이 써요. '탐사 저널리즘', '황색 저널리즘'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 탐사 저널리즘은 오랜 시간 조사해서 숨은 사실을 밝혀내요.
phrases.en: Investigative journalism uncovers hidden facts through long research.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 깊이 조사해서 보도하는 방식을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to reporting based on long, in-depth investigation.

phrases.example: 자극적인 제목만 쓰는 황색 저널리즘을 비판하는 사람이 많아요.
phrases.en: Many people criticize yellow journalism that only uses sensational headlines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실보다 자극적인 내용으로 관심을 끄는 보도를 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize reporting that grabs attention with sensationalism over facts.

phrases.en: Reporters must follow journalism ethics.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보도하는 사람이 지켜야 할 기준을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for the standards that people who report news should follow.

explain_en: '언론' often refers to the media or press as a whole, while '저널리즘' is used more for the work of reporting itself and its spirit. It often takes a word in front, as in '탐사 저널리즘' (investigative journalism) and '황색 저널리즘' (yellow journalism).

examples.en: Don't tie grades directly to happiness.

examples.ko: 두 사건을 직결시켜서 생각하면 오해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you link the two incidents directly, you can misunderstand.
The company tied performance directly to pay.
It's a stretch to link those two directly.
They built a road that connects the airport directly to downtown.

examples.ko: 모든 문제를 돈과 직결시킬 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: You don't need to link every problem directly to money.

explain: 원인과 결과나 두 일을 바로 이어서 생각하거나 만들 때 써요. 주로 '~을 ~와 직결시키다' 꼴이고, 너무 단순하게 연결한다는 안 좋은 느낌으로 쓸 때도 많아요. 스스로 이어진다는 '직결되다'와 달라요.

phrases.example: 돈과 행복을 바로 직결시킬 수는 없어요.
phrases.en: You can't directly link money and happiness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 곧바로 이을 수 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say two things cannot simply be tied together.

phrases.example: 실패를 능력 부족과 직결시키는 것은 위험해요.
phrases.en: It is risky to link failure directly to a lack of ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 단순하게 이어서 생각하는 일을 비판할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to criticize thinking that connects things too simply.

phrases.en: I don't tie looks directly to personality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 따로 생각한다는 자기 생각을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state your view that two things should be kept separate.

explain_en: Used when you link two things directly in thought or in practice, in the form '~을 ~와 직결시키다', and often implies the link is too simple. It differs from 직결되다, where things are connected by themselves.
